title.en: Eight killed in plane crash at remote Alaskan military site, air force says
title.zh: 空军称，阿拉斯加偏远军事基地的飞机失事造成八人死亡

summary.en: It is unclear why the civilian-contracted plane was at the radar site on Alaska's south-west coast.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A plane crash at a remote US Air Force site in Alaska has killed all eight people on board, the US military has said.

The civilian-contracted aircraft crashed shortly after midday local time (20:00 GMT) on Thursday near Cape Newenham, which hosts the airport of a long-range radar site.

It is unclear who the other passengers were or why they were there, but the US Air Force Alaskan Command chief said they had been "dedicated professionals carrying out a vital mission in a demanding environment".

"This is a devastating loss for our military family and the communities we serve," Lt Gen Robert Davis added.

"Our absolute priority right now is providing unwavering support to their families, friends and teammates during this devastating time," he said in a statement.

"We are profoundly grateful for the swift and tireless response of our search and recovery professionals."

The plane originally took off from Anchorage International Airport and was bound for Cape Newenham - 450 miles (725 km) to the west by air - the US Air Force Alaskan Command said.

Rescuers who landed near the crash site "confirmed there were no survivors", it added. An investigation is under way and the deceased will be named once their next of kin had been informed.

The plane was chartered by the USACE, which said on Friday it had confirmed two its employees were aboard. The vast majority of the USACE's workforce are civilians and not enlisted soldiers.

Clint Johnson, the chief for the National Transportation Safety Board's Alaska region, said there had been two pilots and six passengers on board, CBS News, the BBC's US partner, reported.

The Cape Newenham site on Alaska's south-west coast is part of the Alaska Radar System, a network of remote sites that monitor aircraft approaching or operating in Alaskan airspace.
body.zh: 美国军方表示，阿拉斯加美国空军一处偏远基地发生的飞机失事已造成机上八人全部遇难。 这架民用飞机于当地时间周四中午（格林威治标准时间 20:00）后不久在纽恩纳姆角附近坠毁，该角设有一个远程雷达站点。 目前尚不清楚其他乘客是谁，也不清楚他们为何在那里，但美国空军阿拉斯加司令部司令表示，他们是“在严苛环境中执行重要任务的敬业专业人员”。 罗伯特·戴维斯中将补充说：“这对我们的军人家庭和我们服务的社区来说是毁灭性的损失。” 他在一份声明中说：“我们现在的绝对首要任务是在这个毁灭性的时刻为他们的家人、朋友和队友提供坚定不移的支持。” “我们对搜索和救援专业人员的迅速而不懈的反应深表感谢。” 美国空军阿拉斯加司令部表示，这架飞机最初从安克雷奇国际机场起飞，飞往纽恩纳姆角——距西边 450 英里（725 公里）。 声明补充说，降落在坠机地点附近的救援人员“确认没有幸存者”。调查正在进行中，一旦通知死者的近亲，将公布死者的姓名。 这架飞机是由美国陆军工程兵团包租的，该公司周五表示已确认机上有两名员工。美国陆军工程兵团的绝大多数员工都是平民，而不是现役士兵。 据英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，国家运输安全委员会阿拉斯加地区负责人克林特·约翰逊表示，机上有两名飞行员和六名乘客。 阿拉斯加西南海岸的纽恩纳角站点是阿拉斯加雷达系统的一部分，该系统是一个远程站点网络，用于监视接近或在阿拉斯加领空运行的飞机。

title.en: Several injured after sword attack at Swedish school
title.zh: 瑞典学校持刀袭击多人受伤

summary.en: Police say one man has been arrested, while several other local schools have been locked down.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Several people have been injured after a sword attack at a high school in Sweden, local authorities say.

Police said they had arrested one man after the incident at Brinell School in Fagersta, central Sweden.

Officers were called to the scene just after 14:00 local time (13:00 BST) on Friday, with some reports in Swedish media saying the suspect was shot in the leg by police.

Fagersta council did not specify the number of wounded, but said police were searching the building and that eight other schools had been placed under lockdown measures.

The Vastmanland region, where Fagersta is located, has declared a state of high alert following the attack.

In a post on X, Sweden's Prime Minsiter Ulf Kristersson described the attack as a "serious incident," and said "we do not know what lies behind the act, but we know that police are working very intensively".

Students at Brinell School had only just returned to the classroom following the summer break, with the new term beginning either on Monday or Wednesday this week, depending on the academic year.

The school has just under 500 students on its roster, according to Sweden's public broadcaster SVT, and is located 170km (105 miles) north-west of the capital, Stockholm.

Sweden has experienced a number of attacks on educational institutions in recent years.

The country experienced it's worst-ever mass shooting in 2025 , where 11 people, including the gunman, died at an adult education centre in Orebro.

This led to the government tightening the country's gun laws after it was found that the suspect legally owned four rifles, three of which were found in the school where attack took place.

Two teachers were killed in a violent attack on a secondary school in Malmo in 2022 - an 18-year-old student later confessed to the attack.

In 2015, a teacher and a pupil were killed in a sword attack at a school in Trollhattan .
body.zh: 地方当局称，瑞典一所高中发生持剑袭击事件，造成多人受伤。 警方表示，在瑞典中部法格斯塔的布内尔学校发生事件后，他们逮捕了一名男子。 当地时间周五 14:00（英国夏令时 13:00）刚过，警方接到报警赶到现场，瑞典媒体的一些报道称，嫌疑人的腿部被警方开枪射中。 法格斯塔议会没有具体说明受伤人数，但表示警方正在搜查该建筑，另外八所学校已采取封锁措施。 法格斯塔所在的西曼兰地区在袭击发生后已宣布进入高度戒备状态。 瑞典总理乌尔夫·克里斯特森 (Ulf Kristersson) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中将此次袭击描述为“严重事件”，并表示“我们不知道该行为背后的原因，但我们知道警方正在非常紧张地开展工作”。 布内尔学校的学生暑假结束后才刚刚回到教室，新学期根据学年的不同，将于本周周一或周三开始。 据瑞典公共广播公司 SVT 报道，该学校名册上有不到 500 名学生，位于首都斯德哥尔摩西北 170 公里（105 英里）处。 近年来，瑞典经历了多起针对教育机构的袭击。 2025 年，该国经历了有史以来最严重的大规模枪击事件，包括枪手在内的 11 人在厄勒布鲁的一个成人教育中心死亡。 这导致政府在发现嫌疑人合法拥有四支步枪后收紧了该国的枪支法，其中三支是在袭击发生的学校中发现的。 2022 年，马尔默一所中学发生暴力袭击，造成两名教师死亡，一名 18 岁学生后来承认了这起袭击事件。 2015年，特罗尔海坦一所学校的一名教师和一名学生在持刀袭击中丧生。

title.en: Iran's president: Time to end war in 'position of strength'
title.zh: 伊朗总统：是时候在“强势地位”下结束战争了

summary.en: Iranian media report that President Masoud Pezeshkian stated it would be a good time to end the war with the US, as Iran is in a "position of strength and dignity." He further added that Tehran would never "bow to intimidation."
summary.zh: 据伊朗媒体报道，总统马苏德·佩泽什基安表示，现在是在“强势地位和尊严”下结束与美国战争的好时机。他还补充说，德黑兰绝不会“屈服于恐吓”。

body.zh: 伊朗媒体援引马苏德·佩泽什基安的话说，现在是结束与美国的战争的好时机，“因为我们处于强大和尊严的地位”。他还表示，德黑兰永远不会“屈服于恐吓”。 据官方媒体报道，伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安周五表示，现在是寻求结束与美国的战争的最佳时机。 他在一次医学会议上发表上述言论之际，德黑兰官员和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普就这场冲突发出了混杂的信息。 六月达成的部分休战协议仍处于看似模棱两可的状态，周一到期，没有任何进展或续签。 德黑兰继续严格限制通过霍尔木兹海峡的航运，而美国则试图对伊朗港口实施所谓的封锁。 特朗普本周威胁要加大对伊朗的经济压力。但美国还能对这个世界上受制裁最严厉的国家之一施加多大的压力，而美国与这个国家几乎没有任何业务往来，目前还不清楚。 正如佩泽什基安似乎暗示的那样，这可能是进行和平谈判的好时机，一位伊朗军事领导人威胁说，如果美国确实试图在经济上进一步孤立伊朗，将采取“毁灭性、惩罚性和毁灭性的反应”。 据伊朗伊斯兰共和国通讯社报道，佩泽什基安表示，战争最终必须结束。 他说：“最好今天就结束这一切，因为我们拥有力量和尊严。” 佩泽什基安说：“全世界都承认我们的胜利，并强调美国违反所有规定袭击了我们的学校、医院和基础设施，受到全世界的仇恨。” 他还认为，伊朗和美国 6 月签署的 15 点谅解备忘录摇摇欲坠，这绝不意味着伊朗的失败。 他说：“他们在这一承诺中甚至找不到任何表明投降的条款。” “所有的承诺都与对方有关。” 虽然大多数人担心的是美国，但 15 项承诺中的少数确实将责任归咎于伊朗，尽管德黑兰可能会辩称，这些承诺只是同意回到战前的状况。最值得注意的例子是允许至少暂时免费通过霍尔木兹海峡进行商业运输，以及伊朗重申不会采购或发展核武器。 据报道，佩泽什基安还告诉医生群，“在任何情况下我们都不会屈服于恐吓”，如果有必要，伊朗将抵抗“直到我们最后一口气”。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普几天后主要发表有关朝鲜半岛和朝鲜领导人金正恩的言论，并简短地回应了他的...

title.en: ‘Shouldn’t be renamed at all’: senator attacks Navy’s reported consideration of honoring Trump instead of Black war hero – live

summary.en: A senator and retired Navy officer criticized reports that the Navy is considering naming an aircraft carrier after former President Trump, potentially replacing plans to honor World War II hero Doris Miller, a Black sailor who distinguished himself during the attack on Pearl Harbor.
summary.zh: 一位参议员兼退役海军军官批评了海军考虑将一艘航空母舰以美国前总统特朗普的名字命名，这可能会取代原计划以二战英雄、在珍珠港袭击中表现英勇的黑人水兵多里斯·米勒的名字命名该舰的报道。

body.en: Mark Kelly, an Arizona Democrat and retired Navy officer, slams Navy’s mulling of naming a carrier for Trump instead of WWII hero Doris Miller US navy carrier set to honor Black war hero may reportedly be renamed after Trump Sign up for the US Breaking News email The NAACP has weighed in on efforts by the Trump administration to strip the name of a Black WWII hero from a carrier under construction. “Doris Miller earned his place in American history through courage, sacrifice, and service. Donald Trump only wants to serve himself,” said NAACP president Derrick Johnson . This is a slap in the face to every war hero and every service member who has worn the uniform. It’s beyond comprehension for a president to want his own name on a Navy ship while our armed forces are living in deteriorating conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. For generations, millions of Black women and men have proudly served in the United States military, defending freedoms that too often were not even afforded to them, their families, or their communities. Donald Trump is making a mockery of that legacy by treating military service as another opportunity for personal branding. Our brave service members signed up to defend the nation, not the fragile ego of one man. America deserves better than this. Continue reading...
body.zh: 亚利桑那州民主党人、退役海军军官马克·凯利猛烈抨击海军考虑以特朗普而非二战英雄多丽丝·米勒命名一艘航母。 据路透社报道，在美国上诉法院周五维持下级法院针对调查的禁令后，司法部针对纽约总检察长利蒂西亚·詹姆斯办公室的传票仍被封锁。詹姆斯对唐纳德·特朗普及其家族企业以及全国步枪协会提起民事诉讼，这两家公司在随后的审判中都被认定负有责任。据路透社当时报道，特朗普于 2025 年上任后，司法部开始轮流调查詹姆斯，对与这些案件相关的潜在侵犯公民权利的行为启动刑事调查。继续阅读...

title.en: Corruption charges dropped against South Africa's police intelligence boss
title.zh: 对南非警察情报部门负责人的腐败指控被撤销

summary.en: Officials had faced charges over the appointment of a civilian to a top post within crime intelligence.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
South African prosecutors have withdrawn fraud and corruption charges brought against criminal intelligence chief Lt-Gen Dumisani Khumalo and six other police officers.

He and his colleagues were arrested in June 2025 over the allegedly unlawful appointment of a civilian to a key post within the intelligence unit. They denied the charges and were not suspended.

The case against them was now been formally dropped at a court in the capital, Pretoria, after a review last month by the country's chief prosecutor.

South Africa's police force has long been plagued by issues of political interference, alleged corruption and a seeming inability to effectively tackle high levels of crime.

A major judicial inquiry into alleged police corruption, known as the Madlanga Commission, is currently under way.

It was established last year by President Cyril Ramaphosa after a senior police officer alleged that organised crime groups had infiltrated the government.

Speaking outside court in Pretoria after the withdrawal of the charges, Gen Khumalo expressed relief that the "truth at least is out".

Prosecutors had claimed that Dineo Mokwele was unqualified for the senior technical support services position she held within crime intelligence and labelled her a "token appointment".

It heard that Mokwele was more than qualified for the post and had about a dozen certificates to her name.

In July, Andrea Johnson - the former head of a specialised unit within the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) tasked with investigating high level and complex corruption cases - appeared before the commission.

She admitted that she was unaware of Mokwele's qualifications and apologised for remarks made about her.

Gen Khumalo became the head of Crime Intelligence in 2022. Up until then, he had served in different police units for more than two decades.
body.zh: 南非检察官撤回了对刑事情报局长杜米萨尼·库马洛中将和其他六名警察提出的欺诈和腐败指控。 他和他的同事于 2025 年 6 月因涉嫌非法任命一名平民担任情报部门的关键职位而被捕。他们否认了这些指控，也没有被停职。 经过该国首席检察官上个月的审查后，针对他们的案件现已在首都比勒陀利亚的一家法院正式撤销。 南非警察部队长期以来一直受到政治干预、涉嫌腐败以及似乎无力有效应对高发犯罪率等问题的困扰。 一项名为“马德兰加委员会”的针对警察腐败指控的重大司法调查目前正在进行中。 去年，在一名高级警官指控有组织犯罪团伙渗透到政府后，总统西里尔·拉马福萨成立了该机构。 撤销指控后，库马洛将军在比勒陀利亚法庭外发表讲话，表示“至少真相大白了”，这让他松了口气。 检察官声称迪内奥·莫克韦勒不具备担任犯罪情报部门高级技术支持服务职位的资格，并给她贴上“象征性任命”的标签。 听说莫克韦勒完全有资格担任这个职位，并且拥有大约十几张证书。 7 月，国家检察机关 (NPA) 内负责调查高级别和复杂腐败案件的专门部门前负责人安德里亚·约翰逊 (Andrea Johnson) 出现在委员会面前。 她承认她不知道莫克韦勒的资格，并为针对她的言论道歉。 库马洛将军于 2022 年成为犯罪情报部门负责人。在此之前，他已在不同的警察部门服务了二十多年。

title.en: Ex-Abercrombie & Fitch chief fit to stand trial in sex trafficking case, judge says
title.zh: 法官称前 Abercrombie & Fitch 首席执行官适合在性交易案件中受审

summary.en: Jeffries was declared "mentally incompetent" by a court last year and said to be suffering with dementia and late onset of Alzheimer's disease.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Former CEO of Abercrombie & Fitch Mike Jeffries is competent to stand trial on sex trafficking and prostitution charges, a federal court has ruled, reversing an earlier decision.

Jeffries was declared "mentally incompetent" by a court last year and said to be suffering with dementia and late onset of Alzheimer's disease.

Based on an examination of his medical records and more than 21 hours of audio recordings across 109 calls, Judge Nusrat Choudhury has now ruled that there was "ample evidence" to show that he was fit to stand trial.

Jeffries faces over a dozen charges related to sex trafficking in violation of interstate prostitution. His trial is scheduled to begin on 26 October.

Judge Choudhury said in the 150-plus page ruling that the audio recordings of phone calls were "particularly illuminating".

"On the calls, Jeffries is a fluent conversational partner and shows that he has the ability to learn new information auditorily," Judge Choudhury said. "Jeffries clearly possesses a rational and factual understanding of the proceedings to adjudicate his criminal charges."

The judge said the court would still make certain accommodations, in light of Jeffries 81 years of age and cognitive impairments.

The court will be held from 13:00-17:00, so that Jeffries may use the morning to review transcripts and discuss developments from the previous day.

Trial will also include "at least two or three 15-minute breaks" and both parties will be required to provide full transcripts each day for Jeffries' review.

"To be clear, Jeffries is competent to proceed regardless of these accommodations," Judge Choudhury said.

In October 2024, Jeffries, his partner Matthew Smith, 62, and their alleged middleman James Jacobson, 73, were charged with running a global sex trafficking and prostitution business.

They have pleaded not guilty to the charges. A guilty verdict would carry a maximum sentence of life in prison.

Their arrests followed an October 2023 BBC investigation and ongoing podcast series that revealed the trio had been at the centre of a sophisticated operation scouting young men for sex around the world while Jeffries was CEO of Abercrombie & Fitch.
body.zh: 联邦法院推翻了先前的裁决，裁定 Abercrombie & Fitch 前首席执行官迈克·杰弗里斯 (Mike Jeffries) 有能力接受性交易和卖淫指控的审判。 去年，杰弗里斯被法院宣布为“精神上无行为能力”，并据称患有痴呆症和迟发性阿尔茨海默病。 根据对他的医疗记录和 109 个电话中超过 21 小时的录音的检查，努斯拉特·乔杜里 (Nusrat Choudhury) 法官现已裁定，有“充分的证据”表明他适合接受审判。 杰弗里斯面临十多项与违反州际卖淫行为的性贩运相关的指控。他的审判定于 10 月 26 日开始。 乔杜里法官在 150 多页的裁决中表示，电话录音“特别有启发性”。 乔杜里法官说：“在电话中，杰弗里斯是一位流利的对话伙伴，并表明他有能力通过听觉学习新信息。” “杰弗里斯显然对裁决他的刑事指控的程序有理性和事实的理解。” 法官表示，鉴于杰弗里斯已经 81 岁了，并且有认知障碍，法院仍会做出一定的调整。 法庭将于 13:00-17:00 开庭，以便杰弗里斯可以利用上午的时间查看笔录并讨论前一天的进展情况。 审判还将包括“至少两到三个 15 分钟的休息时间”，双方都必须每天提供完整的笔录供杰弗里斯审查。 乔杜里法官说：“需要明确的是，无论这些安排如何，杰弗里斯都有能力继续进行。” 2024 年 10 月，杰弗里斯、他 62 岁的伴侣马修·史密斯 (Matthew Smith) 以及他们所谓的中间人 73 岁的詹姆斯·雅各布森 (James Jacobson) 被指控经营全球性贩运和卖淫业务。 他们对这些指控表示不认罪。有罪判决最高可判处终身监禁。 他们被捕之前，BBC 于 2023 年 10 月进行了一项调查，并且正在进行的播客系列节目显示，在杰弗里斯担任 Abercrombie & Fitch 首席执行官期间，这三人一直处于在世界各地寻找年轻男性进行性行为的复杂行动的中心。

title.en: 40 years after the Lake Nyos disaster in Cameroon
title.zh: 喀麦隆尼奥斯湖灾难 40 年后

summary.en: On August 21, 1986, a silent cloud of carbon dioxide swept through villages around Lake Nyos in Cameroon, killing nearly 2,000 people in their sleep. Four decades later, survivors are still living with the trauma.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On August 21, 1986, a silent cloud of carbon dioxide swept through villages around Lake Nyos in Cameroon, killing nearly 2,000 people in their sleep. Four decades later, survivors are still living with the trauma.

"The Lake Nyos disaster took everybody by surprise. We had no warning signals before it ever took place," said Isaac Konfor Njilah, a Cameroonian geologist and head of a laboratory in the department of Earth Sciences at the University of Yaounde.

On the night of August 21, 1986, Lake Nyos suddenly released a massive cloud of carbon dioxide that spread through nearby valleys and villages. The gas replaced oxygen, suffocating people and animals as they slept.

Located in Cameroon's Northwest Region, about 315 kilometers (196 miles) northwest of Yaounde, Lake Nyos sits inside an ancient volcanic crater in the Oku volcanic field. At the time of the incident, the area's population exceeded 3,000, with many families relying on farming and cattle ranching.

The disaster claimed the lives of about 1,700 people and some 3,500 head of livestock, making it one of the deadliest natural disasters in Cameroon's history.

Following the disaster, scientists from Cameroon and abroad launched extensive investigations to determine what had happened.

They concluded that carbon dioxide from deep underground had been accumulating at the bottom of the lake for years, trapped beneath more than 200 meters (656 feet) of water.

Before the disaster, the upper layers of the lake contained oxygen-rich water, while the deeper layers were saturated with dissolved carbon dioxide. Njilah explains that water has an insatiable appetite for carbon dioxide.

"So when carbon dioxide comes from the [Earth's] mantle, it is being dissolved continuously in the lake," Njilah told DW.

Scientists often compare Lake Nyos to a giant bottle of carbonated water. For decades, carbon dioxide built up in the lake's depths. When that balance was disturbed, the gas escaped in a rapid chain reaction, releasing a deadly cloud that rolled through nearby communities.

Researchers believe a landslide may have triggered the release by disturbing the gas-rich waters at the bottom of the lake.

Carbon dioxide is harmless at normal atmospheric levels. But in high concentrations, it acts as an asphyxiant, displacing oxygen in the air. Because the gas is heavier than air, it flowed downhill into villages, where many residents died in their sleep before realizing anything was wrong.

The Nyos tragedy was not a first in Cameroon. Two years earlier, on August 15, 1984, a similar event occurred at nearby Lake Monoun, about 100 kilometers southeast of Nyos. A sudden release of carbon dioxide killed 37 people.

body.zh: 1986年8月21日，一股二氧化碳云无声无息地席卷了喀麦隆尼奥斯湖周围的村庄，导致近2000人在睡梦中丧生。四十年过去了，幸存者仍然承受着创伤。 喀麦隆地质学家、雅温得大学地球科学系实验室主任艾萨克·康福尔·恩吉拉 (Isaac Konfor Njilah) 表示：“尼奥斯湖灾难让所有人都大吃一惊。灾难发生之前我们没有任何预警信号。” 1986年8月21日晚上，尼奥斯湖突然释放出大量二氧化碳云，扩散到附近的山谷和村庄。这些气体取代了氧气，使熟睡的人和动物窒息而死。 尼奥斯湖位于喀麦隆西北地区，雅温得西北约 315 公里（196 英里）处，坐落在奥库火山场的一个古老火山口内。事发时，该地区人口超过3000人，许多家庭以务农和放牧为生。 这场灾难夺去了约1,700人的生命和约3,500头牲畜的生命，使其成为喀麦隆历史上最致命的自然灾害之一。 灾难发生后，来自喀麦隆和国外的科学家展开了广泛的调查，以确定发生了什么。 他们得出的结论是，来自地下深处的二氧化碳多年来一直在湖底积聚，被困在 200 多米（656 英尺）深的水下。 灾难发生前，湖的上层含有富氧水，而深层则充满了溶解的二氧化碳。尼吉拉解释说，水对二氧化碳有着无法满足的胃口。 恩吉拉告诉德国之声：“因此，当二氧化碳来自（地幔）时，它会不断溶解在湖中。” 科学家经常将尼奥斯湖比作一大瓶碳酸水。几十年来，二氧化碳在湖的深处不断积累。当这种平衡被打破时，气体会发生快速的连锁反应，释放出致命的云，席卷附近的社区。 研究人员认为，山体滑坡可能通过扰乱湖底富含气体的水域而引发释放。 二氧化碳在正常大气水平下是无害的。但在高浓度下，它会起到窒息剂的作用，取代空气中的氧气。由于气体比空气重，它顺着山坡流入村庄，许多居民在意识到问题之前就在睡梦中死去。 尼奥斯悲剧在喀麦隆并不是第一次发生。两年前，即 1984 年 8 月 15 日，尼奥斯东南约 100 公里处的莫努恩湖附近也发生了类似的事件。突然释放的二氧化碳导致 37 人死亡。 科学家们仍在调查莫农灾难，当时更致命的......

title.en: Ukraine's farmers struggle to sell harvest amid war, drought
title.zh: 乌克兰农民在战争和干旱中艰难出售收成

summary.en: Russian attacks on ships and ports in the Black Sea are threatening Ukraine's agricultural sector. Grain exports are severely restricted, and Kyiv is seeking solutions.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Russian attacks on ships and ports in the Black Sea are threatening Ukraine's agricultural sector. Grain exports are severely restricted, and Kyiv is seeking solutions.

Russian attacks on civilian ships have effectively brought the ports in the greater region of Odesa to a standstill. Until recently, they handled about 90% of Ukraine's agricultural exports.

The Ukrainian government has been working on finding alternative routes via rail, road and other waterways. It is also currently in negotiations about an export corridor that would go via Moldova .

But many experts have pointed out that these temporary alternatives cannot replace the ports, and warn that the current blockade of the Black Sea is an even greater threat to the Ukrainian economy than that posed by  Russia's full-scale invasion of 2022.

The strained security situation in the Black Sea is already having a palpable effect on Ukraine's domestic market. According to Denys Marchuk, the deputy chairman of the All-Ukrainian Agrarian Council, Ukrainian farmers have already harvested more than 28 million tons of grains and pulses .

But a large part of this harvest cannot be sold, which has led to a shortage of the cash needed to complete the harvest and to plant winter crops. Planting usually begins at the end of August in Ukraine's southern regions.

"Right now, we can barely sell our harvest. Instead, we're storing what we have harvested — that's if we find storage space. At the same time, we are wondering what to do because we need money, especially so we can plant in fall," Marchuk told DW.

He predicted that the situation would continue to worsen in the coming weeks and months when grain and oilseed crops, which are usually harvested later, compounded the crisis. 

The corn harvest alone could reach about 33 million metric tons this year. Yet in the coming months, there could be a shortage of storage capacity totaling up to 10 million tons. Regions on the front, where most silos have been destroyed amid the ongoing war, are particularly affected.

"You often hear that farmers want to leave their corn in the fields to be harvested in spring. It still needs to be dried, which needs a lot of electricity that is very expensive. They don't have the money," said Marchuk. "There aren't enough places where they can sell it, nor are the prices reasonable, so for them it makes more sense to leave it in the fields as that's cheaper."

Maksym Hopka, an analyst at the Ukrainian Agribusiness Club, estimates that Ukraine's agricultural output totaled about 3.7 million metric tons in July, of which about 2.7 million metric tons comprised grain. That was a decline of about a quarter in comparison to the previous month. He expected an additional fall of over 50% in August.

title.en: North Korea: Will Trump-Kim talks happen anytime soon?

summary.en: As Donald Trump claims a meeting is planned with Kim Jong Un, North Korea's response sends a signal that it wants maximum concessions in return for talks with the US.

body.en:
As Donald Trump claims a meeting is planned with Kim Jong Un, North Korea's response sends a signal that it wants maximum concessions in return for talks with the US.

North Korea responded on Thursday to claims by US President Donald Trump that he will be holding talks with leader  Kim Jong Un later in the year with a broadside of ballistic missiles .

The South Korean military said Pyongyang launched 10 short-range missiles that landed in the sea off North Korea's east coast. 

This came a day after Kim's powerful sister, Kim Yo Jong, said Pyongyang was "completely unaware of" plans for discussions.

Trump's announcement on Wednesday that he is in contact with Kim and that the two leaders would meet later in the year appears to have caught Pyongyang off guard. It comes after the US president said the military would scale back annual military drills with South Korea.

The statement by Kim Yo Jong, director of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea and one of her brother's closest advisers, dismissed Trump's decision to dramatically scale back the 10-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises as "unworthy of comment and [we] have no interest in it at all."

"After Trump's overtures, Kim Yo Jong effectively said downscaling exercises is not enough, and North Korea launched about a dozen missiles in its third firing in two weeks," Leif-Eric Easley, a professor of international studies at Ewha Womans University in Seoul, told DW.

In a statement carried by the state-run Korea Central News Agency (KCNA), Kim Yo Jong mocked South Korea as a "puppet" and indicated that only canceling the drills in their entirety would be seen as a "goodwill measure."

Choo Jae-woo, a professor of foreign policy at South Korea's Kyung Hee University, told DW that unlike in Trump's first term, Pyongyang right now is in a position of power and will likely seek more guarantees before coming to the negotiating table.

"North Korea is not interested in dialogue because Kim was humiliated in 2019 when Trump walked out of their talks in Hanoi," said Choo said.

Those talks ended in acrimony over the US insistence that North would have to scrap its nuclear program.

Pyongyang has since forged a close security and economic alliance with Russia , granting it access to military technology, energy and consumer goods previously beyond its grasp under international sanctions.

"They are in the safe hands of Russia and China and, in the years since Hanoi, Kim has made it his regime's official position that North Korea will never engage in dialogue as long as giving up its nuclear weapons is part of the discussion,” Choo added.

title.en: What Europe's shrinking rivers reveal, and why Australia should take notice
title.zh: 欧洲河流萎缩揭示了什么，以及澳大利亚为何应引起关注

summary.en: Discoveries from Europe's shrinking rivers highlight environmental challenges that extend globally, prompting other regions like Australia to observe and learn.
summary.zh: 欧洲河流萎缩所揭示的发现，指出了远远超出该大陆的挑战。

body.en:
In northern Bulgaria, water in the Danube River has fallen so low that scientists say an ancient mammal has once again been exposed to the world.

The remains of what is believed to be a woolly mammoth were uncovered in late July and hailed by historians as a "very important" discovery.

Near the Serbian village of Prahovo, the rusted vessels and broken masts of German warships also resurfaced from the riverbank this month.

"This has literally never happened before; these wrecks ... have never been visible like this. They've always been completely submerged; what we're seeing now is utterly unprecedented," he said.

The discoveries along Europe's second-longest river come as parts of central and eastern Europe experience prolonged summer heatwaves and drought conditions.

Armin Fojskic, a member of the Zenica Fishermen Association, said if conditions don't ease, he expects a large number of fish to die in European rivers.

"Low levels of water are critical for the fish, especially if it is extremely low, and these past days it has really been extremely low," Fojskic said.

"The main danger for fish is oxygenation of the river; when water flow drops, the river loses oxygen and fish start to suffocate."

According to the European Drought Observatory, about half of Europe and the United Kingdom experienced drought at various levels of intensity in July. Major wildfires have also burned across the continent .

But Peter Gleick, a hydro-climatologist and co-founder of the Pacific Institute in California, believes what Europe has experienced is not in line with normal weather fluctuations.

"Weather is always variable. We always have droughts. We always have floods somewhere at some time ... but what we're seeing now is extreme events worsened by human-caused climate change," Gleick told SBS News.

"We're dumping greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. We know that's warming the planet. We know that it's altering these extreme events by making them more extreme, more frequent, and more intense."

Gleick said the extreme patterns affecting rivers in Europe are similarly impacting water systems across the globe.

"In the western United States, the Colorado River, which is ... shared by seven [US] states and Mexico, is at record low levels," he said.

"Some of the largest reservoirs in the world are built on the Colorado River, and they're now at record lows."

Nick Bond, the director of freshwater ecosystems at La Trobe University, said the Murray-Darling Basin, Australia's largest river system, has been in decline for decades .

summary.en: Former US President Donald Trump's independent foreign policy actions, including reducing military drills and engaging with North Korea, have led Asia-Pacific allies to express doubts about the reliability of US defense agreements.
summary.zh: 美国前总统唐纳德·特朗普的独立外交政策行动，包括削减军事演习和与朝鲜接触，导致亚太盟友对美国防务承诺的可靠性产生疑问。

body.en:
Donald Trump's recent appeals to the reclusive North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un have cast doubt on the United States' commitment to its allies in Asia and the Pacific — potentially adding to regional instability, experts worry.

Trump has also reignited fears about North Korea's nuclear test program and whether the US would ever back down on opposing the nation's weapons, which would have broad ramifications.

A decision by the US on Monday to "substantially reduce" the scope of ongoing joint military exercises with South Korea and Japan may have sent a ripple of doubt about the strength of the many interlinked defence ties in the region, and caught some off guard.

Trump announced the decision on social media , saying the exercises were costly and "send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile" to North Korea. The totalitarian state had previously complained about the joint military drills, saying they would respond with a new level of deterrence.

But the decision, which came somewhat out of the blue, was made at the same time as Trump is signalling plans to meet with the North Korean leader, raising questions about where their unusual relationship actually sits.

South Korean president Lee Jae Myung said on Wednesday he recognised Trump's "will and efforts to create conditions for dialogue" with North Korea through the reduction of the exercise.

"President Trump's message this time feels like a major decision made with careful consideration to create peace on the Korean Peninsula, moving beyond hostility and confrontation," he wrote on social media.

Joshua Kurlantzick, senior fellow for Southeast Asia and South Asia at the US think tank the Council on Foreign Relations, told SBS News the US decision was in one way unsurprising, given its stated foreign policy shift away from global hegemony and toward influence over the "Western hemisphere" alone.

"As a result, and this includes Australia, they are taking various measures." He said this includes strengthening regional defence ties and increasing military spending.

body.en:
The Fijian government will introduce a new tourism services tax for large-scale tourism operators next month, with travel industry experts warning that the costs could be passed on to customers.

The 5 per cent tax will apply from 1 September. The change has been criticised by travel associations in Fiji, Australia and New Zealand, who claim they were not properly consulted.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) said the measure could catch out travellers who have already booked trips to Fiji from September onward, as travel agents and operators face confusion over how to administer the tax.

"The design and roll out reflect a complete lack of understanding of how the travel booking ecosystem works, and it is travellers and travel businesses who will pay the price for that failure," ATIA CEO Dean Long said.

"Travellers are the ones left exposed. Families with September school holiday bookings already paid in full, and travellers on large group, corporate and film production bookings, are being asked to find extra money for a holiday they thought was settled months ago. That is not how you treat people who chose Fiji in good faith."

The change forms part of wider taxation amendments enacted as part of Fiji's 2026-2027 national budget, passed last month.

According to Fijian finance minister Esrom Immanuel, revenue from the tax will be used to support Fiji Airways.

"The revenue generated will be ring-fenced and fully directed to Fiji Airways, which continues to face financial pressure from rising aviation fuel costs and its ongoing recovery from losses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic," Immanuel told local media in June.

It's reported that the tourism tax will generate around FJ$70 million ($44.7 million) for the airline. The Fijian government is the largest shareholder of Fiji Airways.

ATIA confirmed it will meet with the Fijian government to discuss the tourism services tax, which it said arrived with "zero consultation".

Long said there is ongoing confusion over how the tax is collected, saying that members of the travel industry in Australia and New Zealand — which represent Fiji's largest tourism markets — were not consulted on the change.

"None of this needed to happen. The tax arrived with zero consultation with the travel industry in Australia or New Zealand despite the significant importance of these markets to Fiji," he said.

Türkiye, Egypt and Qatar, which have been trying to ‌mediate an end to the Gaza Strip conflict, have condemned recent Israeli strikes in the ‌Palestinian enclave, urging Israel to meet its ceasefire obligations and avoid steps that could ‌escalate tension.

United States envoy Jared Kushner wrapped up a regional visit ‌on Monday amid attempts to advance US President ⁠Donald Trump's plan to end the war.

summary.en: Three activists in Hong Kong have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under a national security law introduced by China.
summary.zh: 香港三名活动人士根据中国实施的国家安全法，被判煽动他人颠覆国家政权罪名成立。

body.en:
Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils to commemorate the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under the city's controversial national security law.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison after being convicted under the China-introduced law. Sentencing is expected at a later date.

Lee and Chow "incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", according to a summary on Friday. Chow told the court in May the law itself was on trial.

Hong Kong used to be one of the only places in Chinese territory where people could gather to mark the deadly 1989 crackdown against pro-democracy protesters.

Authorities banned these gatherings in 2020, citing Covid-19 policies, but they have never resumed. This was also the year the national security law, which makes illegal a wider range of dissenting acts, officially came into force.

In mainland China, authorities have banned even oblique references to the 1989 crackdown.

In the courtroom, Chow smiled as the verdict was read out, while Lee showed little emotion as he made a heart gesture and folded his hands to show his gratitude to those in the gallery.

Lee, a lawmaker, and Chow, a lawyer, were also leaders of the now-defunct Hong Kong Alliance (HKA), which has been described as a "toxic tumour" by Chinese authorities.

The HKA was founded in May 1989 to support students holding pro-democracy rallies. Weeks later, the Communist Party crushed pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square with troops and tanks. Estimates of the death toll range from a few hundred to many thousands.

Over the next three decades, HKA called on authorities to accept responsibility for the crackdown, free dissidents and introduce democratic reform.

Rights group Amnesty International has said the case "relies on vague, overly broad and arbitrary definitions of 'subversion'".

Sarah Brooks, Amnesty International's deputy regional director, said Chow and Lee had "not committed any recognisable crime".

"Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan are prisoners of conscience who should never have been prosecuted in the first place. They must be released immediately and unconditionally," she added.

Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, said the convictions showed "how public displays of mourning have become a crime in Hong Kong".

In a separate case, Chow was arrested in June 2021 for "inciting" the public to take part in that year's vigil and later found guilty.

title.en: Hong Kong convicts Tiananmen vigil leaders
title.zh: 香港将天安门守夜活动领导人定罪

summary.en: The two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists were found guilty of inciting subversion. The high-profile case has been widely criticized for highlighting the deterioration of freedom of expression.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists were found guilty of inciting subversion. The high-profile case has been widely criticized for highlighting the deterioration of freedom of expression.

A Hong Kong court on Thursday convicted two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists under Beijing's  controversial national security law for "incitement to subversion."

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, had organized candlelight vigils to mark Beijing's deadly 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. They were charged in 2021 and both pleaded not guilty.

They face a maximum prison term of 10 years and are expected to be sentenced at a later date.

Germany and France on Friday morning  published a joint statement to say that both "deeply regret the guilty verdict against human ​rights lawyer and democracy activist Chow Hang-tung."

The statement called for the immediate release of Chow and added that "peaceful advocacy for human rights does not constitute a crime."

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council, which oversees the island's China policy, expressed "deep regret and sorrow" and called on the Chinese Communist Party and Hong Kong government to "immediately release those detained in this case." 

Hong Kong judicial officials claimed the pair "incited other persons to organize, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power."

Prosecutors had argued they "endanger(ed) national security in the name of human rights."

Public commemorations of the deadly Tiananmen crackdown , when Beijing sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital's Tiananmen Square, have been effectively banned since the 2020 imposition of the national security law on Hong Kong.

The controversial law came after Hong Kong's massive anti-government, pro-democracy protests in 2019.

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 中国正准备执行二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务

summary.en: China is preparing its most ambitious moon mission in two decades, scheduled for next month. The mission aims to explore the lunar surface, specifically searching for water.
summary.zh: 中国正准备在下个月执行其二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务。此次任务旨在探索月球表面，特别是寻找水资源。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

"Indonesia must also exercise caution in this regard," she said, adding that Jakarta should "not to be too naive," to assume that its participation in a "regular exercise" with China would not cause concern in...
body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The family of slain Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom say they will continue their fight for justice, with missing drone audio remaining one of the central unanswered questions about her death.

Israel this week announced it would not prosecute those responsible for the killing of Frankcom and six of her World Central Kitchen colleagues in Gaza in April 2024, despite conceding "serious failures" that led to the mistaken-identity drone strikes by the Israel Defense Force (IDF) .

On Thursday, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the decision was an "outrage" , and she had no confidence in the IDF's Military Advocate General's two-year investigation "given the many unanswered questions".

Among the unresolved issues is a missing piece of drone footage audio, which Israel refused to hand over to Australia's independent inquiry, headed by retired Air Chief Marshal Mark Binskin, despite requests by the federal government.

According to his report — which found the killing was due to mistaken identity and procedural failings but not a deliberate targeting of aid workers — Binskin was given access to 90 minutes of unedited drone footage, but it did not include an audio track.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese renewed calls for the audio to be released in parliamentary Question Time on Thursday, saying it's part of the transparency Australia has called for "from day one".

Israeli ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman on Friday told ABC radio the audio may contain "intelligence information" and there was nothing in it to cast doubt on the findings which cleared the IDF of criminal misconduct.

In a statement on Thursday, Frankcom's family called on the government to continue pressing Israel to release the audio and to "pursue all available legal avenues for an independent and credible investigation to be conducted".

However Dr Emily Crawford, an international law professor at the University of Sydney, said Australia's options were limited.

"In all states, the scope to argue that national security grounds required for information not to be released, they're fairly paramount," she told SBS News.

"We've seen that the Netanyahu government is reluctant to assist in these kinds of things, so I can't imagine there's really going to be any movement on that."

title.en: What Europe's shrinking rivers reveal, and why Australia should take notice

summary.en: Discoveries from Europe's shrinking rivers highlight environmental challenges that extend globally, prompting other regions like Australia to observe and learn.

body.en:
In northern Bulgaria, water in the Danube River has fallen so low that scientists say an ancient mammal has once again been exposed to the world.

The remains of what is believed to be a woolly mammoth were uncovered in late July and hailed by historians as a "very important" discovery.

Near the Serbian village of Prahovo, the rusted vessels and broken masts of German warships also resurfaced from the riverbank this month.

"This has literally never happened before; these wrecks ... have never been visible like this. They've always been completely submerged; what we're seeing now is utterly unprecedented," he said.

The discoveries along Europe's second-longest river come as parts of central and eastern Europe experience prolonged summer heatwaves and drought conditions.

Armin Fojskic, a member of the Zenica Fishermen Association, said if conditions don't ease, he expects a large number of fish to die in European rivers.

"Low levels of water are critical for the fish, especially if it is extremely low, and these past days it has really been extremely low," Fojskic said.

"The main danger for fish is oxygenation of the river; when water flow drops, the river loses oxygen and fish start to suffocate."

According to the European Drought Observatory, about half of Europe and the United Kingdom experienced drought at various levels of intensity in July. Major wildfires have also burned across the continent .

But Peter Gleick, a hydro-climatologist and co-founder of the Pacific Institute in California, believes what Europe has experienced is not in line with normal weather fluctuations.

"Weather is always variable. We always have droughts. We always have floods somewhere at some time ... but what we're seeing now is extreme events worsened by human-caused climate change," Gleick told SBS News.

"We're dumping greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. We know that's warming the planet. We know that it's altering these extreme events by making them more extreme, more frequent, and more intense."

Gleick said the extreme patterns affecting rivers in Europe are similarly impacting water systems across the globe.

"In the western United States, the Colorado River, which is ... shared by seven [US] states and Mexico, is at record low levels," he said.

"Some of the largest reservoirs in the world are built on the Colorado River, and they're now at record lows."

Nick Bond, the director of freshwater ecosystems at La Trobe University, said the Murray-Darling Basin, Australia's largest river system, has been in decline for decades .

Two women at the centre of an investigation involving five players from the Sydney Swans AFL club were subjected to "abhorrent" actions, the women's lawyer alleges, further stating that they fear for their lives.

John Karantzis, acting for two of the three women involved, says more than five men were in the hotel room and accuses Swans hierarchy of not yet being fully transparent.

Sydney banned five players — Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon — for the rest of the AFL season for breaching club standards at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel on Monday morning.

Victoria Police Sex Crimes Squad detectives are investigating. No charges have been laid.

Karantzis said more than five men were in the room but refused to comment when asked if other Swans staff members were present.

"We have every reason to consider that reports to the contrary are simply false," the statement said.

Cox conceded he and other club leaders needed to take responsibility for rebuilding the Swans' reputation.

"I've been at the football club for nine years. Every person within those four walls we value extremely highly and they have a massive say on our culture as a group," he said.

"We understand as leaders we need to lead that culture, but what we are going to do is back ourselves, and we're going to move forward and we're going to strive as strongly as we possibly can to repay the faith."

"With what has been alleged, these women were subjected to the most disgusting actions and behaviour I have ever heard about in my 28 years as a lawyer," he said.

"And what they were subjected to, it is alleged, was demeaning, abhorrent and simply not moral or acceptable."

body.en:
The Fijian government will introduce a new tourism services tax for large-scale tourism operators next month, with travel industry experts warning that the costs could be passed on to customers.

The 5 per cent tax will apply from 1 September. The change has been criticised by travel associations in Fiji, Australia and New Zealand, who claim they were not properly consulted.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) said the measure could catch out travellers who have already booked trips to Fiji from September onward, as travel agents and operators face confusion over how to administer the tax.

"The design and roll out reflect a complete lack of understanding of how the travel booking ecosystem works, and it is travellers and travel businesses who will pay the price for that failure," ATIA CEO Dean Long said.

"Travellers are the ones left exposed. Families with September school holiday bookings already paid in full, and travellers on large group, corporate and film production bookings, are being asked to find extra money for a holiday they thought was settled months ago. That is not how you treat people who chose Fiji in good faith."

The change forms part of wider taxation amendments enacted as part of Fiji's 2026-2027 national budget, passed last month.

It will affect tourism operators — including hotel, tourism and cruise businesses — with an annual turnover above FJ$2 million (approximately $1.3 million).

According to Fijian finance minister Esrom Immanuel, revenue from the tax will be used to support Fiji Airways.

"The revenue generated will be ring-fenced and fully directed to Fiji Airways, which continues to face financial pressure from rising aviation fuel costs and its ongoing recovery from losses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic," Immanuel told local media in June.

It's reported that the tourism tax will generate around FJ$70 million ($44.7 million) for the airline. The Fijian government is the largest shareholder of Fiji Airways.

ATIA confirmed it will meet with the Fijian government to discuss the tourism services tax, which it said arrived with "zero consultation".

Long said there is ongoing confusion over how the tax is collected, saying that members of the travel industry in Australia and New Zealand — which represent Fiji's largest tourism markets — were not consulted on the change.

summary.en: Half a million Australians are said to be exposed amid "significant uncertainty" about funding for the sector.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Half a million Australians have no access to desperately needed drug and alcohol addiction help, and funding uncertainty is intensifying the risk to existing services, a peak health provider warns.

The Australasian Therapeutic Communities Association (ATCA) fears that funding for many services is "a house of cards" that will collapse if federal funding is cut or not renewed.

ATCA chair Gerard Byrne said its members, who provide residential therapy, outreach and day programs, were reporting increases in waiting lists and waiting times.

"They turn up in hospitals, in police stations, in courts, in prison, in homeless services, in domestic and family violence services," he said.

"But they're not going there for the drug and alcohol problem. They're going there because all of those other things were happening for them because they couldn't get the drug and alcohol service."

ATCA executive officer Michelle Ridley said half a million Australians needing drug and alcohol treatment were missing out, and the issue was most acute in regional and remote areas.

"There is significant uncertainty about future funding for the sector and without confirmation of ongoing funding, some services undoubtedly face very hard decisions about their future admissions," she said.

"Our members are operating in an environment of significant pressure due to increasing demand for alcohol and other drug treatment services, workforce challenges, and uncertainty about future funding arrangements.."

Following a review of the federal Drug and Alcohol Program, the federal government extended existing grants until the end of June 2027.

Byrne said the sector needed the grant opportunities for the next round of three-year grant agreements to be released soon.

"The uncertainty is in what the future will be after the application process, because we're funded up until June 2027, but our members don't know what's happening after that," he said.

"DAP funding usually part funds programs along with the state and territory governments, so you get this house of cards situation where if you take one funding stream away or reduce it, the other funding streams are at risk because the financial sustainability is not there."

Readers struggling with their use of alcohol and other substances can contact the National Alcohol and Other Drug Hotline on 1800 250 015 for free and confidential support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. More information is available via Lifeline .

reflection.en: This story draws attention to hope, endurance, and faithful rebuilding. Romans 12:12 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with steady hope and perseverance, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到盼望、忍耐与重建。Romans 12:12提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以坚定盼望与忍耐来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。
